lessons.title: What the game is about
lessons.objective: You can say in one sentence how a team wins.

payload.prompt: How many points is a touchdown worth?

explanation.correct: Six points for the touchdown itself. After that, the team gets one or two bonus points with an extra-point try.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is six points by itself. The kick or two-point play after the touchdown adds one or two more.
explanation.sayThisLine: Six for the touchdown, then one or two more.

payload.prompt: Tap the end zone where touchdowns happen.

diagram.alt: A football field with yard lines marked every 10 yards, with end zones at each end painted differently from the main field.

explanation.correct: Right. Each end zone is 10 yards deep. Getting the ball into either end zone for a touchdown is worth six points.
explanation.incorrect: The end zones are the 10-yard areas at each end of the field, past the goal lines. That is where touchdowns happen.
explanation.sayThisLine: The end zones are in the corners; that is where you score touchdowns.

payload.prompt: In football, which team scores a touchdown: the one with the ball or the other team?

scene.alt: Two football teams on a field, one with the ball near the end zone.

explanation.correct: The team with the ball is the offense. They score the touchdown. After, the other team (defense) gets the ball back.
explanation.incorrect: The offense (team with the ball) scores touchdowns by getting into the end zone. The defense tries to stop them.
explanation.sayThisLine: The team with the ball scores when they get into the end zone.

payload.prompt: Match these concepts to what they mean in football.

pairs.definition: The 10-yard area at each end of the field where a team scores a touchdown.
When a team has the ball and controls play.
When the offense gets the ball into the end zone; worth six points.

explanation.summary: These three ideas tie together: possession is having the ball, and scoring a touchdown means getting it into the end zone.
explanation.sayThisLine: Ball in hand, get to the end zone, that is six points.

payload.prompt: Tap the player who would score a touchdown if he gets to the end zone.

diagram.alt: A football field with a player holding the ball near the defense, teammates ahead near the end zone, and defenders behind.

explanation.correct: Any player on the offensive team with the ball who gets into the end zone scores. That includes whoever has the ball or catches it in the end zone.
explanation.incorrect: Only the team with the ball can score a touchdown. Either the runner or a receiver in the end zone would get the points.
explanation.sayThisLine: The player holding or catching the ball in the end zone is the one who scores.

lessons.title: The field and the line
lessons.objective: You can point to the end zone, yard lines and the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: Tap where the line of scrimmage is before a play starts.

diagram.alt: A football field showing offense and defense lined up, with the line where the teams face off marked clearly.

explanation.correct: The line of scrimmage is where the ball is placed. The offense and defense line up on opposite sides of it to start the play.
explanation.incorrect: The line of scrimmage is the imaginary line where the ball sits before the snap. Both teams line up along it.
explanation.sayThisLine: The line of scrimmage is where both teams face off at the start of the play.

payload.prompt: Fill in the yard line markers on a football field.
payload.template: The football field is {{length}} yards long from end zone to end zone. Yard lines are marked every {{increment}} yards. The middle of the field is at the {{middle}} yard line.

explanation.correct: A football field is 100 yards long between the end zones, with yard lines marked every 10 yards. The 50-yard line is the middle, dividing the field in half.
explanation.incorrect: From end zone to end zone is 100 yards. Yard lines mark every 10 yards, making the 50-yard line the center.

payload.prompt: Each end zone adds 10 yards to the field length. True or false?

scene.alt: A full football field with end zones shaded differently at each end, showing the total length including end zones.

explanation.correct: True. The playing field is 100 yards, but each end zone is 10 yards, so the total field is 120 yards long.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, the field itself is 100 yards, but the end zones at each end add 10 more yards each for a total of 120 yards.
explanation.sayThisLine: The playing field is 100 yards, plus a 10-yard end zone at each end.

payload.prompt: Point to where the 40-yard line is on the field.

diagram.alt: A football field with all yard lines labeled from 0 to 50 to 100, showing the full field with yard markers.

explanation.correct: The 40-yard line is 40 yards from the end zone in that direction. The yard lines count up from 0 at the end zone to 50 at midfield on each side.
explanation.incorrect: Each yard line is labeled with its distance from the nearest end zone. The 40-yard line is 40 yards away.

payload.prompt: Match field terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: The yard line where the ball is placed before each play; where offense and defense face off.
Marked lines on the field every 10 yards to show field position and distance.
The 10-yard area beyond the goal line where a team scores a touchdown.

explanation.summary: The field has yard lines to track position, a line of scrimmage where plays start, and end zones where touchdowns are scored.
explanation.sayThisLine: Yard lines show where you are; the line of scrimmage starts the play; end zones are where you score.

lessons.title: Four downs
lessons.objective: You can explain what a down is and why fourth down matters.

payload.prompt: What is a down in football?

options.text: When a player falls to the ground
One of four tries the offense gets to move the ball

explanation.correct: Exactly. A down is one play or attempt. The offense gets four of them to move the ball 10 yards.
explanation.incorrect: A down is one play attempt. The offense has four tries (four downs) to advance the ball 10 yards or more.
explanation.sayThisLine: A down is one play; the team gets four tries to move the ball.

payload.prompt: Fourth down is the team's last chance to keep the ball and keep moving. True or false?

scene.alt: A field showing downs counting 1, 2, 3, 4 with a ball carrier getting closer to the goal line.

explanation.correct: True. If they do not make 10 yards by the end of the fourth down, they give the ball to the other team.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, if the offense does not make 10 yards by fourth down, it is turnover on downs and the other team gets the ball.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth down is your last chance; if you do not get 10 yards, you lose the ball.

payload.prompt: Complete this sentence about down and distance.
payload.template: Third and {{distance}} means it is the {{down}} down, and the team needs {{yards}} more yards to get a new set of downs.

explanation.correct: Third and seven means it is the third down, and the team needs 7 more yards to get a first down. They have one more try if they do not make it.
explanation.incorrect: Down and distance tells you which play it is and how many yards are needed. Third and seven means 3rd down needing 7 yards.

payload.prompt: Match down terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: One play attempt. The offense has four tries to move the ball 10 yards.
When the offense gains 10 yards, they get four new downs and keep the ball.
A phrase like third and seven, telling which down it is and yards needed for a first down.

explanation.summary: Downs let the offense try to move the ball. Get 10 yards in four attempts and you earn a new set of four.
explanation.sayThisLine: Four tries to move the ball 10 yards; make it and you get four more.

payload.prompt: The offense can keep playing forever if they always get first downs. True or false?

scene.alt: A field showing offensive plays advancing the ball and gaining first downs repeatedly.

explanation.correct: True. As long as they keep gaining 10 yards every four downs, they can move down the field indefinitely until they reach the end zone.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, that is the idea. Keep making first downs and you can drive all the way for a touchdown.
explanation.sayThisLine: Every first down resets your four tries, so you can keep moving if you gain 10 yards each time.

lessons.title: Where is the first down?
lessons.objective: You can read the yellow line and say if they got the first down.

payload.prompt: A team starts at their 20-yard line and gains 8 yards. Did they get a first down?

scene.alt: A field marking the 20-yard line as the starting position and the 28-yard line as the ball position after a run.

explanation.correct: No. They needed 10 yards and only gained 8. They are at 2nd and 2 on the next play.
explanation.incorrect: No, they needed 10 yards to get a first down. Moving 8 yards leaves them short.
explanation.sayThisLine: Eight yards is not enough when you need 10, so no first down yet.

payload.prompt: Tap where the chains crew would place the marker for a first down.

diagram.alt: A football field showing the ball position, the line where it started, and the yellow first down marker chain 10 yards away.

explanation.correct: The first down marker is placed 10 yards ahead of the line of scrimmage. If the ball reaches this marker, it is a first down.
explanation.incorrect: The chains crew uses a marker chain to mark the first down line, which is 10 yards from the line of scrimmage.

payload.prompt: Sometimes they use the chains to measure if the offense got a first down. True or false?

scene.alt: A football field with officials and the chains crew measuring the exact distance between the ball and the marker.

explanation.correct: True. When it is very close, officials bring out the chains to measure exactly if the ball reached the first down marker.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, a measurement chain is brought out to see if the offense gained exactly 10 yards and earned a first down.
explanation.sayThisLine: When it is close, they measure with the chains to see if you got the first down.

payload.prompt: If the ball is here and the first down marker is there, does the offense have a first down?

diagram.alt: A field showing the ball position past the first down marker with officials confirming the gain.

explanation.correct: If the ball touches or goes past the marker, it is a first down. The offense gets four new downs.
explanation.incorrect: The ball must reach the first down marker. If it does, the offense gets a new set of four downs.

payload.prompt: Match first down terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: A chain placed 10 yards ahead of the line of scrimmage to show where a first down is earned.
When officials use the chains to see if the ball gained exactly 10 yards on a close play.
Four fresh downs the offense gets after earning a first down.

explanation.summary: The first down marker shows the goal. Reach it and you get four more downs to keep going.
explanation.sayThisLine: The marker is your target; reach it and you keep your four tries.

lessons.title: The clock
lessons.objective: You can say how long a game is and why it feels longer.

payload.prompt: How many actual minutes does a four-quarter football game last?

explanation.correct: About 180 minutes (three hours). Four quarters of 15 minutes each would be 60 minutes, but the clock stops constantly for incomplete passes, timeouts and penalties.
explanation.incorrect: A four-quarter game typically runs about 180 minutes (three hours) on the clock in real time due to all the stoppages.

payload.prompt: How long is each quarter of a football game?

explanation.correct: Each quarter is 15 minutes of actual play time. Four quarters is 60 minutes of pure game clock.
explanation.incorrect: Quarters are 15 minutes each. But the real time is much longer because the clock stops for many stoppages.

payload.prompt: The play clock is a separate timer that runs between plays. True or false?

scene.alt: A scoreboard showing both the game clock and a shorter play clock counting down.

explanation.correct: True. The play clock gives the team only 40 seconds (or 25 after certain plays) to snap the ball or it is a delay-of-game penalty.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, there is a separate play clock. Teams must start their next play before it runs out, or they lose a down.

payload.prompt: Tap when you think the play clock will run out.

theme.label: Snap before the play clock runs out

explanation.correct: You got the snap off in time. Good timing keeps the offense in rhythm.
explanation.incorrect: You were late. The play clock ran out and it would be a delay-of-game penalty.

payload.prompt: Match clock terms to what they do.

pairs.definition: The main clock that counts down through the quarters. It stops on incomplete passes, fouls and stoppages.
A 40-second timer (25 after some plays) between snaps. Teams must snap before it hits zero.
A team can stop the clock to regroup. Each team gets three per half.

explanation.summary: The game clock runs the quarters, the play clock limits setup time, and timeouts let teams pause for strategy.
explanation.sayThisLine: Game clock runs the quarters, play clock rushes the snap, timeouts let you regroup.

lessons.title: How points happen
lessons.objective: You can add up a score from touchdowns, kicks and safeties.

payload.prompt: Match scoring plays to their point values.

pairs.definition: Six points when the offense gets the ball into the end zone.
Three points when the offense kicks the ball through the uprights.
One point for kicking the ball through the uprights after a touchdown, or two points for a play from the two-yard line.
Two points when the defense tackles the ball carrier in their own end zone.

explanation.summary: Touchdowns are the biggest score. Field goals are worth less. Extra points come after touchdowns. Safeties are rare defensive scores.
explanation.sayThisLine: Six for the touchdown, three for the field goal, one or two for the extra point, two if the defense gets a safety.

payload.prompt: A team scores a touchdown and kicks the extra point. How many total points?

explanation.correct: Seven points: six for the touchdown and one for the kicking extra point. If they scored a two-point conversion instead, it would be eight.
explanation.incorrect: A touchdown is six points. An extra point kick adds one more for a total of seven.

payload.prompt: When does a safety happen?

options.text: When a defender scores a touchdown
When the defense tackles the ball carrier in the end zone
When a player leaves the field without permission

explanation.correct: When the defense tackles the offense in their own end zone, the defense scores two points. It is one of the rarest plays.
explanation.incorrect: A safety is when the defense tackles the ball carrier in the offense's end zone, scoring two points for the defense.

payload.prompt: A field goal is worth more points than a touchdown. True or false?

scene.alt: A kicker attempting a field goal with the ball rising toward the uprights.

explanation.correct: False. A field goal is three points. A touchdown is six, and it is much harder to kick than to score a touchdown.
explanation.incorrect: No, a touchdown is worth six points while a field goal is only three. Touchdowns are the main way to score.
explanation.sayThisLine: Field goals are easier to kick but worth less than touchdowns.

payload.prompt: Match the two ways to score extra points.

pairs.definition: After a touchdown, the team kicks the ball from the 15-yard line for one point.
After a touchdown, run or pass from the 2-yard line for two points instead of kicking.
The team picks whether to try the kick for one or go for the conversion for two.

explanation.summary: After a touchdown, teams choose between an easy kick for one point or a harder play from the 2-yard line for two.
explanation.sayThisLine: You can kick for one or try to score from the 2-yard line for two.

lessons.title: Giving the ball away
lessons.objective: You can say the difference between a fumble, an interception and a punt.

payload.prompt: Match turnover terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: When a defender catches a pass meant for a receiver. The defense takes over the ball.
When a ball carrier drops or loses the ball. Either team can recover it.
When the offense loses the ball to the defense. Interceptions and fumbles are turnovers.
When the offense kicks the ball away on fourth down because they did not gain 10 yards. Not a turnover.

explanation.summary: Interceptions and fumbles are turnovers; the other team gets the ball. A punt is not a turnover; it is an intentional kick.
explanation.sayThisLine: Interceptions and fumbles lose the ball. A punt is just kicking it away on purpose.

statement.speaker: Fan at game
statement.text: Our quarterback threw an interception in the end zone. That was a disaster.

payload.question: What just happened?

options.text: The defense caught the pass meant for a receiver, taking over the ball in great position

payload.translation: An interception in the end zone is the worst turnover: the defense not only got the ball but got it deep in your own territory.

followUps.line: Did the receiver run the wrong route?
followUps.why: Shows you understand communication between quarterback and receiver.

followUps.line: Was that the first interception of the game?
followUps.why: Tests whether you are tracking turnovers as a key stat.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure, ask if interceptions usually happen because of great defense or bad throwing.

payload.prompt: When a running back fumbles, either team can recover the ball and keep it. True or false?

scene.alt: A football play showing a fumbled ball on the ground with players from both teams trying to reach it.

explanation.correct: True. A fumble is a loose ball. Whoever recovers it, offense or defense, gets possession. It is chaos.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, fumbles are loose balls. Either team can pick it up and keep it. That is why fumbles are so chaotic and dangerous.
explanation.sayThisLine: A fumble is live; whoever picks it up keeps the ball.

payload.prompt: A punt on fourth down is a turnover because the other team gets the ball. True or false?

scene.alt: A punter kicking the ball downfield on fourth down in a strategic situation.

explanation.correct: False. A punt is not a turnover. The offense chooses to kick the ball away on fourth down. It is a field position move, not a mistake.
explanation.incorrect: No, a punt is intentional. It is not a turnover; it is a tactical kick to move the ball and flip the field.
explanation.sayThisLine: A punt is not a turnover; it is an on-purpose kick to move the field position.
